title: Shakira and Maluma Reunite on Steamy New Merengue-Fueled Collaboration ‘Agua’: Stream It Now
summary: The Colombian superstars return to their shared musical universe with a sensual merengue fueled by desire, chemistry and tropical heat.
contentText:
Shakira and Maluma are turning up the heat with “Agua,” their new collaboration, released Thursday (Sept. 17). The steamy merengue-fueled single marks the latest chapter in the Colombian superstars’ enduring creative relationship — and their first major duet since 2018’s “Clandestino.”

Produced with a contemporary tropical edge, “Agua” blends Caribbean-rooted rhythm with sleek pop production, creating a soundtrack for surrendering to attraction. Throughout the song, water and thirst become metaphors for overwhelming desire, with the singers acknowledging that their connection is powerful enough to extinguish — or ignite — the fire between them.

“Porque cuando me miras se hace agua la boca / Calmá’ mi sed desde que estás aquí,” they sing in the catchy chorus, translating to: “Because when you look at me, my mouth waters / You’ve quenched my thirst since you’ve been here.” Maluma’s playful, confident verses add another layer of flirtation, while Shakira’s unmistakable vocals bring both sensuality and command to the track.

The accompanying music video, directed by Hannah Lux Davis, builds a glossy, tropical world around the song’s central metaphor. Reflections, liquid surfaces, shimmering light and fluid choreography underscore the magnetic tension between the two artists, who share the same effortless chemistry that powered their previous global hits.

“Agua” follows Shakira and Maluma’s “Chantaje,” “Trap” and “Clandestino,” as well as their collaboration on the remix of Carlos Vives’ “La Bicicleta.” “Chantaje” topped the Hot Latin Songs chart for 11 nonconsecutive weeks and reached No. 51 on the Hot 100, while “Clandestino” reached No. 9 on Hot Latin Songs and topped three Billboard airplay charts.
